_source: Written for the club and committed here because the articles table cannot be written from a developer machine: anonymous INSERT on `articles` is refused by row-level security (42501), which is the security posture working as designed. Only an admin session in Control panel -> News can create one.
_note:
THE SAME DEVICE AS fixtures-2627.json, for the same reason. A piece the club wants published today should not wait on somebody being at a laptop with a login. Each entry LOSES to a stored row with the same slug, so the moment this article is entered in the panel the database copy wins and this one disappears from the build. It cannot produce a duplicate.

The shape is the shape the panel writes: the whole body lives in `lede`, which is how all five existing articles are stored. Anything the panel would store and this file omits simply is not set.
_replaceWhen: Delete an entry once the same article exists in the Supabase `articles` table. Nothing breaks if that is forgotten, because the stored row already wins; the file just carries a copy nobody reads.

data.lede:
League Eight begins on Sunday morning, at home, against Three Little Birds FC. Kick-off is 11am at The Reeves Sports Club on Snakey Lane in Hanworth.

Three Little Birds arrive from a different league. They spent last season in the Metropolitan Sunday Football League and have come across to the Southern Sunday Football League for 26/27. Sunday is a first meeting for both clubs, and neither has a form guide on the other.

That is true of most of the division. Nine clubs make up League Eight, so there are sixteen league matches to play, and of the eight sides in it Sue’s Angels have played only two before: Brockwell Violets, three times, winning all three, and Barnes Stormers once, a 7-0 in the Dylan Rigobert Trophy in February. Pure Football FC 1st Team are new as well. The club beat Pure Football FC 2.0 in pre-season, but that is a different side and no record carries over. Five of the eight have never been met at all.

What came before is on the record and does not need dressing up. Sue’s Angels won League Ten last season having played eighteen, won eighteen, scored ninety and conceded eleven, finishing on fifty-four points. Three of those eighteen were awarded as walkovers and carry no score, which is worth saying out loud, because it is the reason the other fifteen are worth believing. Frazier-Isaías Osunkoya scored thirty-one goals in all competitions and Charlie Dunkley made nineteen assists.

Eleven goals conceded in eighteen league matches is the number that travels least well between divisions, and it is the one the season will test first.

Pre-season was a different story, and a more useful one. Six friendlies, three won, one drawn, two lost, twelve scored and twelve conceded. Five of the six were away from home. The 5-0 at Kingsmeadow United on 12 August is the heaviest defeat in the club’s short history. The last of them, a 4-1 against BPR at The Reeves on 30 August, was the first time this squad had played a home match together.

Twenty-two players are at the club for 26/27. Seventeen of them were here last season and have signed on again; five are new, the most recent being the defender Rob Heath, who joined on 17 August. League Eight is a step up, and the squad that won League Ten has not yet played a competitive match in it.

Everything is on the website: the fixture list, the squad, and every result from the first season onwards. The result and the report from Sunday will be up shortly after full time.

Sue’s Angels FC v Three Little Birds FC · League Eight · Sunday 6 September, 11am · The Reeves Sports Club, Snakey Lane, Hanworth.
data.title: League Eight starts at home to Three Little Birds
